correctness.rationale: For f=id, Peircean transforms are all permutations. Identity axiom II forces [a,e,a] exactly; each unordered size-three multiset on k distinct diversity atoms is independent. For an n-tuple, partition into k nonidentity equality blocks with or without an e block: {n\brace k}+(k+1){n\brace k+1}={n+1\brace k+1}, each multiplied by 2^{binom(k+2,3)}. Fraisse homogeneity/QE identify these quantifier-free patterns with complete types. Injective n-tuples use either all diversity values or one e, so a_n=2^{binom(n+2,3)}+n*2^{binom(n+1,3)}. New nonidentity x over finite A with k diversity atoms introduces exactly 1+k+binom(k+1,2)=binom(k+2,2) independent bits; extension axioms realize all assignments. The lower k<n terms have a Bell(n+1)*2^{-binom(n+1,2)} relative bound and vanish, yielding both limits. Independently exhausted all 0/1 ternary free-cycle tables through k=3 (1,2,16,1024) and checked identity/IP invariance; independently computed n=0..6 p_n and a_n and one-point exponents k=0..8. The experiments corroborate rather than prove the general n formula. Sources: James M. Koussas, Finite Relation Algebras (2021/2022), DOI:10.1017/jsl.2021.81, arXiv:2202.01959; Definitions 7, 9, 26; Propositions 10, 11; Lemma 25; Corollary 27; Definition 28 and Lemma 29.

value.rationale: Exact all-arity orbit/type growth and finite-parameter one-point type spaces of a natural and previously established generic relation-algebra atom structure are meaningful classification invariants. The asymptotic orbit dominance and explicit parameter dependence quantify the qualitative QE/omega-categoricity statement and allow comparisons with other homogeneous structures. The algebraic counting is short and no new model-theoretic existence theorem is claimed; mathematical contribution is limited to exact specialization, not a new general Stirling method.

limitations: Independent finite checks do not establish unbounded n; the proof relies on published Fraisse homogeneity/QE and elementary structural counting.
Finding applies to generic symmetric integral nonassociative relation-algebra atom structures, not counts of finite relation algebras or representable/associative completions.
